findings.body:
`label-gate` (and the matching scope-job checks) rename the dogfood trigger from `ready` to `AIReview`, but that rename is not in the PR summary/test plan and leaves the rest of the repo pointing at `ready`.

Failure mode: after merge, maintainers following `AGENTS.md` (“label-gated on `ready`”), `docs/TRIGGER_MODES.md` (recipe still titled `ready`, still cites this file as the reference), or this PR’s own test plan (“apply the `ready` label”) will not fire self-review. The header comment that points at TRIGGER_MODES § “labelled `AIReview`” is also a broken anchor — that section title is still `ready`.

Fix: either (a) keep `ready` here and only add the complexity inputs, or (b) keep `AIReview` and update `AGENTS.md`, the TRIGGER_MODES recipe/cross-links, and the PR test plan in the same change so the operational contract stays one name.

Comment says chat-completions legs are `(anthropic, codex)` and will apply `complexity:*`, but `codex` is an `AgentRunnerProvider` — same family as `claude-code` / `cursor`.

Failure mode: with `complexity-labels-enabled: true`, the codex leg logs the agent-runner no-op WARNING and never calls `set_pr_complexity` (`docs/PR_METADATA_CHECKS.md` provider matrix; `build_agent_runner_noop_warning` in `scripts/reviewer.py`). Only `provider: anthropic` performs the assessment today. The PR description repeats the same mistake.

```suggestion
          # § `complexity-labels-enabled`. The model calls `set_pr_complexity`
          # and applies `complexity:low|medium|high`. Chat-completions legs
          # (anthropic only) perform the assessment; agent-runner legs
          # (claude-code, cursor, codex) log a no-op warning by design.
          complexity-labels-enabled: true
          complexity-label-prefix: 'complexity:'
```

summary:
## Verdict

Useful dogfood of `complexity-labels-enabled`, but two correctness/docs issues should be fixed before merge — one will mislead operators about which legs label complexity, and one renames the self-review gate without updating the documented contract.

## What looks good

- Enabling `complexity-labels-enabled: true` + default `complexity-label-prefix: 'complexity:'` on the local `uses: ./` path is the right Rule #10 dogfood surface for `docs/PR_METADATA_CHECKS.md`.
- Permissions stay least-privilege (`contents: read`, `pull-requests: write`); no new secrets, no shell interpolation of PR content, no third-party action pin changes.
- Scope/gate empty-reason plumbing (`no-gate-label`) stays internally consistent within the workflow file.
- Complexity labeling itself is best-effort and already guarded for agent-runners via `build_agent_runner_noop_warning` — turning it on here will not break legs.

## Findings

1. **`codex` is not chat-completions** (`.github/workflows/self-review.yml` comment + PR body). Only `anthropic` will apply `complexity:*` today; `codex`/`claude-code`/`cursor` no-op with a WARNING. Fix the comment (and PR description) so the dogfood expectation matches `docs/PR_METADATA_CHECKS.md`.

2. **`ready` → `AIReview` rename is incomplete.** The workflow, gate `if:`, and operator messages all switch, but `AGENTS.md` still says label-gated on `ready`, `docs/TRIGGER_MODES.md` still documents the recipe as `ready` while citing this file as the reference, and this PR’s test plan still says “apply the `ready` label”. That will strand maintainers who follow docs/test plan after merge. Prefer either dropping the rename from this PR or landing the doc/test-plan updates with it.

## Notes (no inline)

- `complexity-label-prefix: 'complexity:'` is redundant with the action default — fine as living docs, not a defect.
- Multi-provider matrix + shared `complexity:*` prefix: last successful chat-completions leg wins the label. Acceptable for dogfood; worth
